title: Code Injection via eval and new Function
platform_conditions: ECMAScript 2020 semantics in Node.js runtime and browsers; identical engine behavior in both
security_mechanism: eval and the Function constructor compile their argument as a full program with the caller's scope chain, so an injected expression is indistinguishable from first-party code and can close over in-scope variables. A string argument to setTimeout/setInterval is the same construction delayed. Node's vm module is frequently mistaken for a sandbox, but its contexts share the process: scripts can reach the host objects via the built-in constructor escape chains (this.constructor.constructor) and exit into require('child_process'). Dynamic require(path) / import(specifier) with attacker text loads attacker-chosen modules from the resolver's search path.

source_sink_clues.source: User-supplied expression or rule strings (template fragments, formula fields, stored 'script' columns), request-derived module names, and persisted strings later handed to eval / new Function / string setTimeout.
source_sink_clues.sink: eval(), new Function(), string-form setTimeout/setInterval, vm.runInNewContext/runInThisContext on untrusted text, dynamic require() / import() with attacker-controlled specifiers

tracking_guards: Check the evaluated text is a compile-time constant and only values are dynamic; check data-shaped inputs are parsed with JSON.parse instead of evaluated; check expression needs are met by a parser/expression library that never calls eval; check dynamic imports resolve from a fixed allowlist of module names.
not_candidate_when: The argument is a literal constant in the shipped code, the input is parsed with JSON.parse (data, not code), or require targets are chosen from a fixed internal map keyed by a validated enum value.
public_references: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html
Node.js documentation: vm module (execution of untrusted code is not its purpose) — https://nodejs.org/api/vm.html
